# ssf-cors

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from servlets/ssf/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/ssf-cors.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `ssf-cors` component of `servlets/ssf`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.servlet.ssf`: generated from its catalogue, ssf-cors.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `SSF` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_SSF_CORS_ORIGINS` (init-param `corsOrigins`, then system property `oidf.ssf.corsOrigins`, then env `OIDF_SSF_CORS_ORIGINS`) | Unset; a list | The browser origins, such as https://console.example, allowed to read the transmitter configuration metadata (/.well-known/ssf-configuration) with GET, space- or comma-separated; unset, no origin is, since receivers fetch it from servers. An origin listed gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin naming it and Vary: Origin; '*' is refused. Until 0.7.0 every origin got Access-Control-Allow-Origin * | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, or an entry that is not http(s)://host[:port] with no path ('*' included): the SSF transmitter is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and its endpoints answer 503. An origin left out is refused by the browser, not by the server | Any | Yes |
